title: Pexeixon: car battle game from my childhood floor, now playable in the browser
author: lashakii
selftext:
When I was a kid, my brother, my best friend and I spent hours smashing Hot Wheels into each other on the floor. No real rules. Just push the other cars until they flip or fall off something.



We called it \*\*Pexeixon\*\*. It comes from "pechação", Brazilian Portuguese slang for cars crashing into each other. I added the "eixon" at the end so it sounded English. I was 7 lol.



I've been a software engineer for about 15 years, and this is the one project I always wanted to make and never finished. I tried Unity. Then Unreal. Then Godot. Then a browser version. Every time, work or life got in the way and it died halfway.

Recently I started using AI to build it (Claude Code, through T3 Code), and it finally clicked. AI generated the code, assets, textures and sound effects. I acted as the director.

Yes, it's "vibe" coded. But I know exactly how it should feel, because I've been thinking about it since I was a kid.   


\*\*How it plays right now\*\*



\- Pull back your car, aim, let go

\- Knock everyone else off the table

\- Last car standing wins

\- Solo vs CPU, local multiplayer, or online rooms with a share link



\*\*Honest status\*\*

It's very much a work in progress and changes almost every day. Some stuff is broken, and the physics still feels off sometimes.



\*\*Play it here:\*\* [https://www.pexeixon.com](https://www.pexeixon.com)



\*\*Stack\*\*

\- Mainly ThreeJS (toy-car physics on everyday arenas)

\- AI coding: Claude Code through T3 Code — agents for systems, UI, and iteration

\- Assets & textures: AI-generated, then curated (using Gemini Pro Image Gen)

\- SFX: AI-generated



\*\*What AI actually helped with\*\*

\- Scaffolding game systems and iterating on features fast

\- Generating art/textures for arenas and cars

\- Generating sound effects

\- Boilerplate + refactors so I could stay on design decisions

  
Looking forward for your feedback! Thank you!
